title: Grounds for Dependency (WIC Section 300)
statement: California Welfare and Institutions Code Section 300 defines the specific circumstances under which a child can be declared a dependent of the juvenile court.
source_says: A child who comes within any of the following descriptions is within the jurisdiction of the juvenile court
steps: Searched 'California Welfare and Institutions Code section 300 dependency grounds text', opened the public.law page for WIC 300, read the opening sentence.

title: Grounds for Dependency (WIC Section 300)
statement: The petition must allege at least one of these grounds:
source_says: The code section and the subdivision under which the proceedings are instituted.
steps: Searched 'WIC 332 petition to commence proceedings must contain', opened public.law WIC 332, read the list of what the petition must contain.

title: Grounds for Dependency (WIC Section 300)
statement: Section 300(a) - Physical Abuse: The child has suffered, or there is substantial risk of suffering, serious physical harm inflicted nonaccidentally by the parent.
source_says: serious physical harm inflicted nonaccidentally upon the child
steps: Opened public.law WIC 300, read subdivision (a). The harm must be inflicted by 'the child's parent or guardian'.

title: Grounds for Dependency (WIC Section 300)
statement: Section 300(b) - Failure to Protect: The child has suffered, or there is substantial risk of suffering, serious physical harm or illness due to the parent's failure to supervise or protect, or the parent's substance abuse.
source_says: The failure or inability of the child's parent or guardian to adequately supervise or protect the child.
steps: Opened public.law WIC 300, read (b)(1). A separate item covers inability to provide regular care due to 'mental illness, developmental disability, or substance abuse.' Note: (b)(2) says a child is not covered only because of homelessness or poverty; the entry does not mention that.

title: Grounds for Dependency (WIC Section 300)
statement: Section 300(c) - Serious Emotional Damage: The child is suffering serious emotional damage, evidenced by severe anxiety, depression, withdrawal, or aggressive behavior toward self or others.
source_says: evidenced by severe anxiety, depression, withdrawal, or untoward aggressive behavior toward self or others, as a result of the conduct of the parent or guardian
steps: Opened public.law WIC 300, read subdivision (c). The law requires the damage to be 'as a result of the conduct of the parent or guardian' or that the child has no parent able to give proper care. The entry leaves that condition out, so it reads as if a child's anxiety or depression alone is a ground.
fix: Section 300(c) - Serious Emotional Damage: The child has serious emotional harm, or is at big risk of it, because of what the parent did, or because no parent is able to give the right care. Signs are severe anxiety, depression, withdrawal, or aggressive behavior.

title: Grounds for Dependency (WIC Section 300)
statement: Section 300(d) - Sexual Abuse: The child has been sexually abused, or there is substantial risk of sexual abuse, by parent or household member.
source_says: by the child's parent or guardian or a member of the child's household
steps: Opened public.law WIC 300, read subdivision (d).

title: Grounds for Dependency (WIC Section 300)
statement: Section 300(e) - Physical Abuse (Under 5): The child is under age 5 and has suffered severe physical abuse by a parent, or by someone the parent knew, when the parent knew or should have known about it.
source_says: The child is under five years of age and has suffered severe physical abuse by a parent, or by any person known by the parent
steps: Opened public.law WIC 300, read the first sentence of subdivision (e).

title: Grounds for Dependency (WIC Section 300)
statement: Section 300(f) - Death of Sibling: The child's parent caused the death of another child through abuse or neglect.
source_says: The child's parent or guardian caused the death of another child through abuse or neglect.
steps: Opened public.law WIC 300, read subdivision (f). Note: the law says 'another child', not only a sibling; the heading 'Death of Sibling' is narrower than the law.

title: Grounds for Dependency (WIC Section 300)
statement: Section 300(g) - No Parental Custody: The child has been left without provision for support and the parent cannot be located.
source_says: The child has been left without any provision for support; ... the child's parent has been incarcerated or institutionalized and cannot arrange for the care of the child; or
steps: Opened public.law WIC 300, read all of subdivision (g). It lists four separate situations joined by semicolons and 'or'. 'Left without any provision for support' stands alone. 'Whereabouts of the parent are unknown' belongs only to the last situation (a relative or other adult caring for the child cannot or will not keep doing so). The entry joins two different situations with 'and' and leaves out the safe-surrender and jailed-parent situations.
fix: Section 300(g) - No One to Care for the Child: Any one of these: the child was left with no support. Or the child was safely surrendered as a newborn and not taken back in 14 days. Or the parent is in jail or an institution and cannot arrange care. Or the adult caring for the child cannot keep doing it and the parent cannot be found.

title: Grounds for Dependency (WIC Section 300)
statement: Section 300(h) - Freed for Adoption: The child has been freed for adoption but placement has not been finalized.
source_says: The child has been freed for adoption by one or both parents for 12 months by either relinquishment or termination of parental rights
steps: Opened public.law WIC 300, read subdivision (h). The entry leaves out the 12 months.
fix: Section 300(h) - Freed for Adoption: The child has been freed for adoption by one or both parents for 12 months, or an adoption petition has not been granted.

title: Grounds for Dependency (WIC Section 300)
statement: The child has been subjected to an act of cruelty by the parent.
source_says: The child has been subjected to an act or acts of cruelty by the parent or guardian or a member of the child's household
steps: Opened public.law WIC 300, read subdivision (i). It also covers a parent who failed to protect the child from cruelty the parent knew or should have known about.

title: Grounds for Dependency (WIC Section 300)
statement: Section 300(i) - Cruelty (Criminal)
source_says: The child has been subjected to an act or acts of cruelty by the parent or guardian or a member of the child's household
steps: Opened public.law WIC 300 and checked subdivision (i) for the words 'criminal' or 'crime'. Neither word is in (i). The label '(Criminal)' has no basis in the text and could make a parent think a criminal charge or conviction is needed.
fix: Section 300(i) - Cruelty

title: Grounds for Dependency (WIC Section 300)
statement: Section 300(j) - Sibling Abuse: The child's brother or sister has been abused or neglected, and there is a substantial risk that this child will be abused or neglected too.
source_says: The child's sibling has been abused or neglected, as defined in subdivision (a), (b), (d), (e), or (i), and there is a substantial risk
steps: Opened public.law WIC 300, read the first sentence of subdivision (j).

title: Grounds for Dependency (WIC Section 300)
statement: Section 300 is the law that explains why CPS can take your child or start a court case.
source_says: and the social worker has reasonable cause to believe that the child has an immediate need for medical care or is in immediate danger of physical or sexual abuse
steps: Opened public.law WIC 300: it says which children are 'within the jurisdiction of the juvenile court'. Searched 'section 306 social worker temporary custody immediate danger', opened public.law WIC 306, read (a)(2): taking a child without a warrant needs a Section 300 reason plus an immediate need or danger. So Section 300 alone covers starting a case, not taking a child.
fix: Section 300 is the law that lists the reasons the county can start a court case about your child. To take a child without a court order, the social worker must also believe the child is in danger right now.

title: Grounds for Dependency (WIC Section 300)
statement: The main reasons include: physical abuse, not protecting your child from harm, your substance abuse putting your child at risk, sexual abuse, or serious emotional harm to your child.
source_says: mental illness, developmental disability, or substance abuse.
steps: Opened public.law WIC 300, read subdivisions (a), (b)(1), (c), (d). Each listed reason matches a subdivision.

title: Grounds for Dependency (WIC Section 300)

title: If You Want to Be Included in Your Child's Case
statement: Presumed parent. Your name is on the birth certificate
source_name: California Courts Self-Help Guide; Family Code 7611(c)
steps: Two sources differ. The selfhelp.courts.ca.gov page lists 'Your name is on your child's birth certificate' as a way to qualify. Family Code 7611 (the entry's own citation), opened on public.law, names the birth certificate only in (c): 'After the child's birth, the presumed parent and the child's natural mother have married, or attempted to marry,' and 'the presumed parent is named as the child's parent on the child's birth certificate'. Rule 5.635(c) and the Judicial Council booklet p.31 tie presumed status to a signed voluntary declaration of parentage, not the certificate itself.
fix: You may be a presumed parent if you signed a voluntary declaration of parentage. Being named on the birth certificate may count too. Ask a lawyer.

title: ICWA-030: Notice of Child Custody Proceeding for Indian Child
statement: If your child may be a member of, or eligible for membership in, a federally recognized Indian tribe, the Indian Child Welfare Act (ICWA) provides special protections.
source_says: or (b) is eligible for membership in an Indian tribe and is the biological child of a member of an Indian tribe
steps: Search budget for this run was used up, so I opened law.cornell.edu 25 U.S.C. 1903 directly and read paragraph (4). Being eligible is not enough by itself; the child must also be the biological child of a member. The Judicial Council booklet p.30 says the same. Subsection 2 of this same entry already states the full rule.
fix: If your child is a member of a federally recognized tribe, or can be a member and has a birth parent who is a member, the Indian Child Welfare Act (ICWA) gives special protections.

title: ICWA-030: Notice of Child Custody Proceeding for Indian Child
statement: Placement preferences favor Native family members and tribal members
source_says: a member of the Indian child's extended family;
steps: Opened law.cornell.edu 25 U.S.C. 1915, read (a) and (b). First choice is any member of the child's extended family. 1903(2) defines that as a grandparent, aunt, uncle, sibling, cousin and so on, with no rule that the relative be Native. Next come homes approved by the tribe, then Indian foster homes. The entry's word 'Native' could make a non-Native relative think they do not count.
fix: Placement rules put the child's family first, even family members who are not Native. Next come homes the tribe approves and other Native homes.

title: ICWA-030: Notice of Child Custody Proceeding for Indian Child
statement: Your attorney should file to invoke ICWA protections
source_name: WIC 224.2(a), (c); Judicial Council ICWA resource guide (May 2025)

steps: Opened public.law WIC 224.2 and rule 5.481: the court and county have 'an affirmative and continuing duty to inquire'. Nothing makes a parent or lawyer file a paper for ICWA to apply. The Judicial Council ICWA resource guide says the parent 'must be ordered to complete Parental Notification of Indian Status (form ICWA-020)' at the first court date. No source found for a filing to 'invoke' ICWA.
fix: You do not have to file anything to get ICWA protections. The court and the county must ask about it and look into it. The judge will have you fill out form ICWA-020 about your family's tribal ties. Tell your lawyer so they can make sure this gets done.

source_says: have the child live with me.
steps: Opened form JV-285, item 9. The form does not decide placement: 'It is up to the social worker and the court whether you will be asked to do these things.'

title: JV-285: Relative Information
statement: legal_reference: WIC §309(e); form JV-285 (supports the page)
source_says: to provide information to the social worker and the court regarding the needs of the child.
steps: Opened public.law WIC 309, read (e): it requires a relative information form but does not give the number. Rule 5.534(b)(2) names it: 'Relative Information (form JV-285) or in a letter to the court.'

title: JV-290: Caregiver Information Form
statement: Form JV-290 allows caregivers (foster parents, relatives ...) to provide written information to the court about how the child is doing in their care.
source_says: To the current caregiver, preadoptive parent, community care facility, or foster family agency caring for the child
steps: Opened form JV-290 at the entry's own link ('JV-290 [Rev. September 1, 2020]'). Boxes: 'Foster parent Relative Legal guardian Preadoptive parent', 'Nonrelative extended family member'. Rule 5.534(k)(1) matches.

title: JV-290: Caregiver Information Form
statement: caregivers (... group home representatives)
steps: Opened form JV-290. It never says 'group home'. It names a 'community care facility' and a 'foster family agency', with boxes 'Foster family agency Community care agency Other(specify):'. I did not open a source that says a group home counts as a community care facility, and the search budget for this run was used up.
fix: caregivers (foster parents, relatives, preadoptive parents, or a community care facility or foster family agency caring for the child)

title: JV-290: Caregiver Information Form
statement: It covers the child's health, education
source_says: Current Status of Child's Medical, Dental, and General Physical and Emotional Health
steps: Opened form JV-290, read the headings. Also 'Current Status of Child's Education'.

title: JV-290: Caregiver Information Form
statement: It covers the child's ... behavior, relationship with family, and any concerns.
source_says: Current Status of Child's Adjustment to Living Arrangement
steps: Opened form JV-290 and read every heading: health, education, special education, adjustment to living arrangement, social skills and peer relationships, special interests and activities, other helpful information, recommendation for disposition. There is no heading for behavior or for relationship with family. Low harm; a caregiver can use 'Other Helpful Information'.
fix: It covers the child's health, school, how the child is adjusting to the home, friends and social skills, interests and activities, other helpful information, and what you think should happen next.

title: JV-290: Caregiver Information Form
statement: If you are caring for a child in the dependency system (as a foster parent or relative), you can use this form to tell the court how the child is doing.
source_says: including foster parents, preadoptive parents, relative caregivers, and nonrelative extended family members.
steps: Opened rule 5.534 (k) and form JV-290.

title: JV-290: Caregiver Information Form
statement: Fill it out before review hearings.
source_says: at least five calendar days (or seven calendar days, if filing by mail) before the hearing
steps: Opened form JV-290 and rule 5.534(k)(4): in person 'no later than five calendar days before the hearing', by mail 'no later than seven calendar days before the hearing'. The entry gives no deadline, so a caregiver could turn it in too late. The form also covers permanency hearings and asks for the original and eight copies.
fix: Turn it in to the court clerk at least 5 calendar days before a review or permanency hearing. If you mail it, send it at least 7 calendar days before.

title: JV-290: Caregiver Information Form
statement: legal_reference: CRC 5.534(j); JV-290
source_says: Caregiver notice and right to be heard
steps: Opened rule 5.534 on courts.ca.gov and listed every subdivision. (j) is 'Electronic service address'. The caregiver part, which names form JV-290, is (k) 'Caregiver notice and right to be heard (§§ 290.1-297, 366.21)'. The cited letter points to the wrong part of the rule.
